s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, progressive skin lesion with recent increase in size and symptoms
salient_findings: Itchy plaque on the mid-back
Gradual increase in size over 10 years
Occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding
Well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration
Horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification
key_facts: Female patient in her 60s
Lesion present since childhood
Lesion was pea-sized and asymptomatic for most of her life
Lesion increased in size over the past 10 years
Lesion is itchy
Lesion has occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding
Lesion is a 1.5 × 1.0-cm well-defined erythematous plaque
Lesion has overlying ulceration
Adjoining skin shows lichenification
Histopathological examination revealed a circumscribed tumor
Tumor has multiple papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell–rich stroma
Tumor has atypical cells, mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis

shortlist.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination revealed a circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining and papillary projections, consistent with apocrine gland carcinoma

shortlist.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of a long-standing, slowly growing lesion with recent increase in size and symptoms, and histopathological findings of a circumscribed tumor with atypical cells and necrosis, are consistent with hidradenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Spiradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological features of a circumscribed tumor with papillary projections and vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma, are similar to those seen in spiradenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical cells, mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis in the tumor, although the tumor is well-defined and circumscribed, raises the possibility of squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Eccrine gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical and histopathological features of the lesion, including the presence of a circumscribed tumor with papillary projections and atypical cells, could also be consistent with eccrine gland carcinoma

raw.rationale: The histopathological examination revealed a circumscribed tumor with a continuous apocrine epithelial lining, multiple papillary projections, and atypical cells, which are characteristic features of apocrine gland carcinoma

rejected.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Lack of specific features of hidradenocarcinoma in the histopathological examination

rejected.label: Spiradenocarcinoma
rejected.why: No mention of characteristic spiradenoma-like features in the tumor

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor's histopathological features do not match those of squamous cell carcinoma, which typically shows dermal invasion and a different tumor architecture

rejected.label: Eccrine gland carcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor's apocrine epithelial lining and other features are more consistent with apocrine gland carcinoma than eccrine gland carcinoma
